title: Tool Reference: Booking an Upward Revaluation on a Trade-In Registration
content:
An issued upgrade credit under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes is revalued upward by booking, as its own entry, the increase the traded piece now supports over the credit already standing on the registration. The entry raises the credit available to spend on that registration by the same figure and stands in the registration's history alongside the original credit.

## What the desk does

The desk performs this action itself. The tool `apply_credit_revaluation_37908854` is unlocked and then called by the agent; it books a single revaluation entry against the registration, stamped with the appraiser who revalued the piece and pointing back at the credit entry it revalues, dated the day it is booked.

## Parameters

- `credit_reference` — the reference number of the trade-in registration whose credit is being revalued, written on the customer's upgrade paperwork as TU- followed by six digits; it is read from the trade-in registration lookup.
- `revaluation_amount` — the increase in credit being booked, in USD to 2 decimal places, always a positive figure, given as a plain number with no currency symbol and no thousands separator; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places by half-up arithmetic at the moment of the call.
- `appraiser_code` — the appraiser who revalued the piece, written as APR- followed by three digits, for example APR-042, in upper case with the hyphen kept and no spaces; it is never left empty on a revaluation and is read from the appraisal engagement the revaluation rests on.
- `source_entry_id` — the reference number of the earlier entry on this registration that booked the credit now being revalued; it is read from the registration's entry history.

## What comes back

A one-line confirmation naming the registration reference, the reference number of the revaluation entry just created, the increase booked in USD to 2 decimal places and the credit now available to spend in USD to 2 decimal places. A string beginning "Error" means nothing was written; any other string means the entry stands and the registration has been raised.
